title: Breakfast Sausage Gravy Pizza
seoTitle: Breakfast Sausage Gravy Pizza | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Brunch pie for the late shift
subtitle: Brunch pie for the late shift
description: Brunch pie for the late shift. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Sausage Gravy Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line. Use Shredded cheddar-mozzarella blend as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown breakfast sausage
steps.instruction: Cook bulk sausage in a skillet over medium-high, breaking into small crumbles until fully cooked and browned. Drain grease — greasy gravy splits on the pizza.

steps.title: Make country gravy
steps.instruction: Melt butter in a pot; whisk in flour 1 minute. Whisk in milk and simmer until thick. Stir in half the cooked sausage. Season with salt, pepper, and sage. Gravy should coat a spoon — thin gravy soaks the crust. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Par-bake crusts
steps.instruction: Oil two sheet pans or large rectangular pans. Stretch dough to fit; dock with a fork. Par-bake at 400°F 8 minutes until set but pale — this prevents a soggy breakfast pizza.

steps.title: Top with gravy, sausage, cheese, and eggs
steps.instruction: Spread sausage gravy on par-baked crusts. Scatter remaining sausage and cheese. Crack eggs over the top — space them so each slice gets half an egg.

steps.title: Bake until eggs set
steps.instruction: Bake at 400°F 12–15 minutes until cheese melts and egg whites are set with jammy yolks. Rotate pans once if your oven runs hot in back.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Breakfast Sausage Gravy Pizza onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Cut and serve breakfast pizza
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes, then cut into squares for the hall line. Breakfast Sausage Gravy Pizza — sausage, gravy, eggs, cheese. Not pepperoni night.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut breakfast pizza into squares on sheet trays — eggs should look set, not runny, for grab-and-go.
Keep hot sauce optional on the side; gravy pizza does not need pepperoni backup.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Brunch pie for the late shift. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Breakfast Sausage Gravy Pizza runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
